content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs against the disclosure and the single USER passage in the conversation, and built a full limitation-by-limitation ledger.

input.summary: Full source ledger built and traced. All 22 claims (1-12 apparatus, 13-17 second apparatus, 18-22 method) were traced limitation by limitation to affirmative passages in input/disclosure.md (the USER passage in input/conversation.md is a truncated duplicate of the same text and adds nothing): rail with flat lower face/upper face/longitudinal slot, printed distance marks beside the slot, fixed fence at the first end with a downwardly projecting portion perpendicular to the rail, two-screw releasable mounting in two corresponding holes and reversal by inversion moving the projecting portion to the opposite longitudinal side while the marked face stays up, removable spacer plate with parallel faces changing setback by its thickness without changing separation, two separate guide carriages each with an anti-rotation key in the slot, one cylindrical drill bushing whose bore passes completely through the carriage and registers with the slot, parallel bores perpendicular to the lower face, threaded clamp knob whose shank passes through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail, per-carriage pointers aligned with their bore axes and read against the same marks so the reading difference is the center-to-center spacing, transverse center index at the rail midpoint, shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with that index, the full method of use (select spacing, loosen, slide to a centered reading pair, tighten, place, press fence or spacer against the edge, align on the centerline, drill both bushings, lift away with nothing left attached), the rigid-polymer-or-metal material list, hardened replaceable bushings, and the no motor/battery/sensor/network recitation. All 27 numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94) were checked for one-to-one meaning, for appearance in at least one figure brief, and for agreement between the ledger, the detailed description parentheticals, and each figure's numeral list; no numeral is orphaned, duplicated, or reused for a second part. Every figure brief (FIG. 1-7) was checked against the Brief Description of the Drawings and the detailed description, including the section-line designations: FIG-2 places designation 3 at both endpoints of the line through the second guide carriage 70 and designation 5 at both endpoints of the line through the first guide carriage 50, matching "line 3-3" in FIG-3 and draft/07, "line 5-5" in FIG-5 and draft/07, and the description's statement that FIG. 3 sections the second carriage and FIG. 5 sections the first. Terminology from the brief (rail, fixed fence, guide carriage, drill bushing, clamp knob, clamping shoe, spacer plate, pointer, center index, sight notch) is preserved, no means-plus-function language appears, the cross-reference and government-support sections match the brief's "no priority claim / no federally sponsored research" instruction, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, alternative left unresolved, or internal comment remains anywhere in the draft. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to the inventor, as instructed. Schematic depiction conventions (plain blocks for carriages, a plain round body for each knob, plain rectangular fence body, generic graduation lines, unnumbered V-notch in FIG. 1) were accepted only where the source affirmatively discloses the part and the brief verbalizes no undisclosed functional relationship, and the application text contains no "by way of example" or "any outline" wording added to justify a renderer's choice. Two defects were found, both in FIG-7 and both concerning the pencil centerline 94: the brief adds an orientation and coincidence relationship the inventor never stated, and that added relationship cannot be drawn consistently with the sight notch alignment required by the description and by claims 6, 13, and 18. Everything else in the ledger is supported and internally consistent.

findings.title: FIG-7 asserts an undisclosed orientation and coincidence for the pencil centerline 94
findings.detail: The figure brief fixes the pencil centerline's orientation relative to the rail and makes it coincide with the transverse center index 24 alone. The disclosure never states which way the centerline runs on the workpiece, nor that it coincides with the center index to the exclusion of the sight notch; it states only that the user aligns both features with the centerline. Orientation of a marked line relative to a functional sighting feature, and which feature it passes through, is technical substance about a functional alignment, not a neutral depiction convention, so it may not be supplied by the drafter. No affirmative USER passage describes the centerline's direction or its coincidence with the center index alone.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-7.md): "A centerline 94 is a single straight line drawn on the workpiece 90, running across the band transverse to the length of the rail 10 and coincident with the transverse center index 24, and visible on the workpiece 90 on both sides of the band." Nearest source passage (input/disclosure.md): "The user can align the center index and the sight notch with a pencil centerline on the workpiece before tightening both carriage knobs." The disclosure says nothing further about the centerline's direction, and the draft's own text (draft/08) likewise says only "the user aligns the transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 with the centerline 94 before drilling."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-7.md, replace the centerline paragraph with: "A centerline 94 is a single straight line drawn on the workpiece 90, shown in alignment with both the transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26, and visible on the workpiece 90 beyond the rail 10." Make no other change; no application text is added or broadened.

findings.title: FIG-7 centerline placement cannot depict the sight notch and center index alignment recited in the description and claims 6, 13 and 18
findings.detail: FIG-7 places the transverse center index 24 "at the left part of the fragment" with the centerline 94 coincident with it and running across the band, while the sight notch 26 is at the second end of the rail, longitudinally offset from that transverse line. A view drawn to this brief necessarily shows the sight notch 26 lying off the centerline 94, which directly contradicts the description and the claims requiring the sight notch and the transverse center index to be aligned together with the centerline. FIG. 7 is the only view designated to show these centering features, so the contradiction is not cured elsewhere.
findings.evidence: Candidate figure brief: "A transverse center index 24 is a short straight mark on the upper surface of the rail 10 at the left part of the fragment ... A sight notch 26 is a shallow V-shaped notch formed in the second end of the rail 10 ... A centerline 94 ... coincident with the transverse center index 24." Conflicting application text: draft/08 - "The jig is then slid along the workpiece edge 92 until the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 are aligned with the centerline 94"; claim 6 - "wherein the sight notch and the transverse center index are alignable together with a centerline marked on the front face of the workpiece"; claim 18 - "moving the drilling jig along the straight edge until the transverse center index and the sight notch are aligned with the centerline".
findings.fix: Adopt the FIG-7 wording given in the preceding finding, so that the centerline 94 is drawn in alignment with both the transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 and no orientation relative to the rail is verbalized. Leave draft/08 and claims 6, 13 and 18 unchanged, since they already recite the disclosed relationship.
